title: Romans Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Romans 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ
Grace to you and peace from God our Father
I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all
I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 1:1 begins with Paul introducing himself as a servant of Jesus Christ, which appears before the other events or statements.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:1, Paul was called to be what?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:1 states Paul was 'called to be an apostle.'

questions.question: What was Paul separated unto, according to Romans 1:1?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:1 says Paul was separated unto the gospel of God.

questions.question: What had God promised afore by his prophets, according to Romans 1:2?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:2 refers to the gospel of God as promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:3, Jesus Christ was made of the seed of whom according to the flesh?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:3 states Jesus Christ was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.

questions.question: How was Jesus Christ declared to be the Son of God, according to Romans 1:4?
options: By the resurrection from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: By the resurrection from the dead
questions.explanation: Romans 1:4 says Jesus was declared to be the Son of God with power by the resurrection from the dead.

questions.question: What have we received by Jesus Christ, according to Romans 1:5?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:5 states by Jesus Christ we have received grace and apostleship.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:6, who are among the called of Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:6 says 'Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ,' addressing the recipients in Rome.

questions.question: To whom is the greeting in Romans 1:7 addressed?
options: To all that be in Rome
questions.correctAnswer: To all that be in Rome
questions.explanation: Romans 1:7 specifically addresses 'To all that be in Rome.'

questions.question: What does Paul thank God for in Romans 1:8?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:8 states Paul thanks God for the faith of the recipients, which is spoken of throughout the whole world.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:9, how does Paul serve God?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:9 says Paul serves God with his spirit in the gospel of his Son.

questions.question: Paul makes mention of the recipients in his prayers how often, according to Romans 1:9?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:9 states Paul makes mention of them always in his prayers.

questions.question: Paul requests for a prosperous journey to come to the recipients, according to Romans 1:10.
questions.explanation: Romans 1:10 mentions Paul making request for a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto them.

questions.question: Romans 1:11 states Paul wants to impart what to the recipients?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:11 says Paul desires to impart some spiritual gift, not physical gifts or wealth.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:7, the recipients are called to be what?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:7 describes the recipients as 'called to be saints.'

medium.title: Romans Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Paul express a desire for in Romans 1:12?
options: To be comforted together with the Roman believers
To preach the gospel in Rome
questions.correctAnswer: To be comforted together with the Roman believers
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:12 states that Paul desires to be comforted together with the Roman believers through mutual faith.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:13 promise will happen if someone participates in spreading the gospel?
options: They will have fruit among believers
questions.correctAnswer: They will have fruit among believers
questions.explanation: This is correct because Romans 1:13 mentions Paul's desire to have some fruit among them as he has among other Gentiles.

questions.question: To whom does Paul say he is a debtor in Romans 1:14?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:14 states that Paul is a debtor both to the Greeks and to the Barbarians.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:15 express about Paul's readiness?
options: He is ready to preach the gospel
He is ready to write letters
He is ready to teach in the synagogues
He is ready to be imprisoned
questions.correctAnswer: He is ready to preach the gospel
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:15 states that Paul is ready to preach the gospel to those in Rome.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:16 say about the gospel of Christ?
options: It is a source of shame
It is the power of God unto salvation
It is only for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: It is the power of God unto salvation
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:16 declares that the gospel of Christ is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believes.

questions.question: What is revealed from faith to faith according to Romans 1:17?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:17 states that the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:18, who is the wrath of God revealed against?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:18 indicates that God's wrath is revealed against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men.

questions.question: What is stated in Romans 1:19 about the knowledge of God?
options: It is only for the wise
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:19 explains that what may be known of God is manifest in them, for God has shown it to them.

questions.question: What do Romans 1:20 and Romans 1:21 collectively reveal about people’s response to God?
options: They became vain and darkened in their hearts
questions.correctAnswer: They became vain and darkened in their hearts
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:21 states that people knew God but did not glorify Him and became vain in their imaginations.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:22 say about those who profess to be wise?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:22 states that professing themselves to be wise, they became fools.

questions.question: How does Romans 1:12 connect to Romans 1:13 regarding mutual faith?
options: Both focus on fruit among believers
Both emphasize the need for comfort
Both speak of the power of God
Both mention the importance of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Both focus on fruit among believers
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:12 and 1:13 both emphasize the importance of having fruit among believers.

questions.question: Paul's prayers for the Romans in Romans 1:9 show his commitment to what?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:9 indicates that Paul continually makes mention of the Romans in his prayers, showing his commitment to their faith.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 1:16 states that the gospel is a source of shame.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Romans 1:16 clearly states that Paul is not ashamed of the gospel.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 1:21 indicates that people glorified God as God.
questions.explanation: This is correct since Romans 1:21 states that they did not glorify Him as God.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 1:14 mentions that Paul is a debtor to both wise and unwise.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 1:14 clearly states that Paul is a debtor to both the wise and the unwise.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:23, into what did people change the glory of the uncorruptible God?
options: An image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things
questions.correctAnswer: An image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things
questions.explanation: Romans 1:23 states that people changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, birds, fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

questions.question: What consequence does Romans 1:24 say God gave people because of their lusts?
options: God gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts
God sent a flood upon them
God hardened their hearts to stone
questions.correctAnswer: God gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts
questions.explanation: Romans 1:24 explains that God gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts to dishonour their own bodies between themselves.

questions.question: According to Romans 1:25, what did people exchange the truth of God for?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:25 states that they changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator.

questions.question: In Romans 1:26, what unnatural behavior is said to have been committed by women?
options: They changed the natural use into that which is against nature
questions.correctAnswer: They changed the natural use into that which is against nature
questions.explanation: Romans 1:26 declares that even the women changed the natural use into that which is against nature, leading to vile affections.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:27 describe about men who left the natural use of the woman?
options: They burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly
questions.correctAnswer: They burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly
questions.explanation: Romans 1:27 states that men leaving the natural use of the woman burned in lust one toward another, committing unseemly acts.

questions.question: What kind of mind does God give to those who do not retain Him in their knowledge according to Romans 1:28?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:28 explains that God gave them over to a reprobate mind to do things which are not convenient because they did not retain God in their knowledge.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'apothnēskō' in Romans 1:32 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'apothnēskō' found in Romans 1:32 means 'to die,' referring to the judgment that those who commit such sins are worthy of death.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Romans 1:23 where the glory of God is contrasted with images of man and animals?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:23 uses contrast by juxtaposing the glory of the uncorruptible God with corruptible images of man and animals, highlighting the folly of idolatry.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of idolatry and worship of creation rather than the Creator as in Romans 1:25?
questions.explanation: Psalm 115:4-8 condemns idols made by human hands and worship of created things rather than God, paralleling Romans 1:25's theme of exchanging the truth for a lie.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the consequences of rejecting God’s truth as described in Romans 1:18-32?
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:9-12 describes the coming of the lawless one and people being deceived because they refused to love the truth, similar to the rejection of God's truth and resulting judgment in Romans 1:18-32.

questions.question: What does Romans 1:22 immediately precede in the chapter?
options: Romans 1:23 about changing the glory of God into images
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 1:23 about changing the glory of God into images
questions.explanation: Romans 1:22, speaking about professing wisdom but becoming fools, directly precedes Romans 1:23 which speaks about changing the glory of God into images.

questions.question: Which literary technique is illustrated by the list of sins from Romans 1:29-31?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:29-31 uses cataloguing, an extensive list of sins to emphasize the depth and breadth of unrighteousness among those rejected by God.

questions.question: How does Romans 1:20 function as a theological argument within the chapter?
options: It appeals to natural revelation as evidence of God's existence and power
It introduces the concept of justification by faith
It recounts the history of Israel's covenant
It prophesies the coming of the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: It appeals to natural revelation as evidence of God's existence and power
questions.explanation: Romans 1:20 argues that God's invisible qualities and eternal power are clearly seen through creation, making people without excuse for not honoring Him.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Paul's introduction in Romans 1:1-7?
options: To establish his apostolic authority and greet the believers in Rome
To explain the law of Moses
To describe his previous missionary journeys
To provide a historical overview of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To establish his apostolic authority and greet the believers in Rome
questions.explanation: Romans 1:1-7 introduces Paul as a servant and apostle, called to preach the gospel, and offers grace and peace to the Roman believers.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 1:32, those who commit sins described in the chapter only do so unknowingly without pleasure in them.
questions.explanation: Romans 1:32 states that those who commit such sins not only do them but also have pleasure in them, knowing the judgment of God.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 1:4 teach about the nature of Jesus Christ?
options: Jesus is declared the Son of God by resurrection power
Jesus is a prophet foretelling God's plan
Jesus is solely a man from the seed of David
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is declared the Son of God by resurrection power
questions.explanation: Romans 1:4 states that Jesus was 'declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead,' affirming His divine sonship confirmed through resurrection.

questions.question: What doctrine about the gospel's universal scope is taught in Romans 1:5?
options: The gospel is for obedience to faith among all nations
The gospel is only for the Jewish people
The gospel is a secret revealed only to apostles
The gospel is a political movement
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel is for obedience to faith among all nations
questions.explanation: Romans 1:5 teaches that grace and apostleship were received 'for obedience to the faith among all nations,' indicating the universal call of the gospel beyond ethnic boundaries.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith and righteousness is revealed in Romans 1:17?
options: The righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith
Righteousness is attained by works of the law
Righteousness is only for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith
questions.explanation: Romans 1:17 declares that 'the just shall live by faith,' teaching that righteousness from God is revealed and appropriated by faith, not works, for all who believe.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 1:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18 states 'the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness,' highlighting God's righteous anger against sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 1:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:20 refers to 'the invisible things of him... even his eternal power and Godhead' being clearly seen in creation, showing God's eternal power and divine nature.

questions.question: How does Romans 1:3–4 connect to Old Testament prophecy and the fulfillment of messianic expectation?
options: It declares Jesus as Son of David and Son of God, fulfilling prophecy
It denies Jesus' connection to Davidic lineage
It focuses only on Jesus' human ancestry
It claims Jesus was a new prophet unrelated to the Old Testament
questions.correctAnswer: It declares Jesus as Son of David and Son of God, fulfilling prophecy
questions.explanation: Romans 1:3–4 links Jesus' humanity from David's seed and divine sonship by resurrection, fulfilling the promised Messiah of the prophets.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Romans 1:16–17 prepare for in the broader biblical narrative?
options: Justification by faith as foundational for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Justification by faith as foundational for salvation
questions.explanation: Romans 1:16–17 emphasizes the gospel's power for salvation through faith, preparing the key New Testament doctrine of justification by faith central throughout Scripture.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 1:18 and Romans 1:32 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: God's wrath is revealed against sin and those who approve it are also judged
Sin is excused if people do not know God's judgment
God's wrath is arbitrary and unconnected to sin
Only sinners who confess are subject to God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath is revealed against sin and those who approve it are also judged
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18 reveals God's wrath against ungodliness, and 1:32 states that those who know God's judgment and approve sin share in the condemnation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 1:21 and Romans 1:23 teach about human idolatry and its consequences?
options: Humans reject God’s glory and exchange it for created images, leading to vain imaginations
Idolatry is a neutral act without spiritual consequence
Idolatry honors God by representing Him in visible form
Humans naturally worship God without deviation
questions.correctAnswer: Humans reject God’s glory and exchange it for created images, leading to vain imaginations
questions.explanation: Romans 1:21 describes failure to glorify God and thankfulness, resulting in darkened hearts, and 1:23 shows this leads to idolatry, exchanging divine glory for images of creatures.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 1:25 and Romans 1:28 teach about humanity’s rejection of truth and God's response?
options: Humans exchanged God's truth for lies and were given over to a reprobate mind
God ignores human rejection of truth without consequence
Humans retain God's truth despite rejecting Him
God rewards humans for their pursuit of knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Humans exchanged God's truth for lies and were given over to a reprobate mind
questions.explanation: Romans 1:25 states people changed God's truth into a lie, and 1:28 explains God gave them over to a reprobate mind as judgment for their rejection.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Romans 1:18–32 teaches that God unjustly punishes people for natural desires. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God reveals wrath against ungodliness and unrighteousness where people suppress truth
God punishes natural desires as inherently sinful
God is indifferent to human behaviors
God only punishes those unaware of His laws
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals wrath against ungodliness and unrighteousness where people suppress truth
questions.explanation: Romans 1:18–32 teaches God's wrath is revealed against those who suppress the truth in unrighteousness, including idolatry and moral sins, not natural desires per se.

questions.question: What doctrine about the apostolic mission is taught in Romans 1:14?
options: Paul feels obligated to preach to all peoples, both Greeks and Barbarians
Paul's mission is limited to the Jewish people
Paul rejects preaching to the unwise
Paul focuses only on the wise
questions.correctAnswer: Paul feels obligated to preach to all peoples, both Greeks and Barbarians
questions.explanation: Romans 1:14 expresses Paul's indebtedness to both Greeks and Barbarians, indicating his universal apostolic mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 1:7 regarding God's relationship to the saints?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:7 addresses the 'beloved of God, called to be saints,' emphasizing God's loving relationship with His people.

questions.question: What theological concept is demonstrated by Paul's desire in Romans 1:11 to impart spiritual gifts for the establishment of the saints?
options: Sanctification and edification of the church
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and edification of the church
questions.explanation: Romans 1:11 shows Paul's aim to strengthen believers through spiritual gifts, which relates to the doctrine of sanctification and church edification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human depravity and divine revelation is taught in Romans 1:19 and 1:21?
options: God has shown knowledge of Himself to all, but humans became unthankful and darkened in understanding
Humans have no knowledge of God
God hides Himself from all mankind
Humans fully glorify God by nature
questions.correctAnswer: God has shown knowledge of Himself to all, but humans became unthankful and darkened in understanding
questions.explanation: Romans 1:19 states that what may be known of God is manifest, but 1:21 explains that despite knowing God, humans did not glorify or thank Him, resulting in darkened hearts.
